text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert - HIGH on org=flybridge (org_id=fb-4821) - sustained qps spike on /v1/generate. Active errors: none. Paging SRE rotation.

maria.sre: picking up. seeing org spike -> tokens/sec up 8x, latency p95 -> 1.2s. No error budget burn yet but burst is choking per-tenant queue.

devon-oncall: oncall here. can we confirm whether this is a model-side regression or traffic pattern? any recent deploys to serving?

maria.sre: no recent infra deploys in last 2h. metrics: sustained request rate from flybridge IP pool. Their production job started a heavy backfill.

rachel-sales: FYI I just got a DM from their CSM — they say some customers are seeing degraded responses and timeouts. They want a temporary relief.

luis-ops: quick options: 1) increase org quota (temp) 2) apply per-org soft-throttle to shed background jobs 3) disable non-critical features (summarization pipeline) for that org.

maria.sre: priority is reduce tail latency for interactive users. recommend: apply temporary org_rl bump to let interactive calls through, and simultaneously enable traffic shaping to deprioritize batch endpoints.

devon-oncall: agree. I'll do a conservative quota bump + tag it for rollback. what's current org RL?

maria.sre: current org qps=50, burst=150. spike is ~420 qps. propose set qps=200, burst=500 for 30m then reassess.

luis-ops: I'll stage the change now: `redwoodctl org update --org flybridge --qps 200 --burst 500 --note "temporary surge relief 5312349999"`

incident-bot: deploy started by luis-ops - config-change (config-service). CID: cfg-0a9fd.

rachel-sales: I'll ping their CSM to tell them we've applied a temporary quota bump and are monitoring. Request they pause any non-essential backfills.

maria.sre: luis, also please add a traffic rule to deprioritize `POST /v1/batch/generate` to low priority (route tag: background). That keeps interactive routes responsive.

luis-ops: applying traffic rule: `redwoodctl route update --org flybridge --route "/v1/batch/generate" --priority low --note "background demotion during surge"`

incident-bot: config-change applied successfully. cfg-0a9fd -> finished.

devon-oncall: metrics showing immediate drop in tail latency p99 for `/v1/generate` from 2.8s -> 0.9s. Throughput is still high but interactive success rate improved. Good.

maria.sre: monitoring checks: QPS now ~380, error rate 0.3% (was 0.8%). Keep observing for 15m then plan rollback.

rachel-sales: CSM confirms some customers still see slowdowns but most interactive flows look OK. They agreed to throttle back background jobs.

luis-ops: note: temporary quota bump scheduled to auto-revert in 30m. I'll also attach an incident tag and update runbook. `incident: 5312349999-flybridge-relief`

devon-oncall: handoff: I'll maintain watch for next 20m then escalate to next oncall if still unstable. If errors exceed 1% for 5m, we'll cut qps back and open a ticket with the customer's eng team.

maria.sre: follow-up action items: 1) Ask Flybridge to limit backfills. 2) Add adaptive throttle for batch endpoints (short-term). 3) Postmortem to include why we didn't detect the scheduled job.

rachel-sales: I've asked CSM to schedule a 1:1 with their platform team. They said the backfill was an uncoordinated maintenance run.

luis-ops: logging note: `audit: org update qps 50->200 burst 150->500 by luis-ops at 5312349999`

incident-bot: Reminder: auto-rollback scheduled in 00:25:00 unless updated.

devon-oncall: after 10m stable window, let's extend by another 30m only if Flybridge confirms they will throttle back.

maria.sre: agreed. I'll check SLOs and token-cost impact; also run a quick golden prompt check against warmed caches.

rachel-sales: customer asked for a short summary they can share internally, I'll draft: "Temporary quota increase and background job demotion applied to restore interactive performance. Monitoring active; scheduled rollback in 25m."

luis-ops: recorded. if we hit error spike again we'll consider feature-disable: `--disable summarization` for that org as last resort.

incident-bot: Auto-rollback executed at 5312350250 - config reverted to qps=50 burst=150 for org=flybridge.

devon-oncall: seeing metrics post-rollback: drop in throughput to expected ~60 qps, latency stable. Error rate remains low.

maria.sre: please coordinate postmortem. Root cause: uncoordinated backfill from customer. Recommend adding an org-level admission control rule and alert when >2x usual daily qps surge.

rachel-sales: CSM confirmed Flybridge will add throttles on their side and coordinate maintenance windows. They appreciated the quick mitigation. :thumbsup:

luis-ops: closing incident. tagging with `live-mitigation`, `org-rate-adjust`, `customer-communication`.

maria.sre: filing follow-up doc in #postmortems with timeline and metrics.

devon-oncall: handing off to next oncall, I'll add notes to the incident ticket.

flybridge-support: (external) thanks for the help — we'll update you once we've reconfigured our backfill jobs.

maria.sre: resolved.
